text.headline: Timeline of France
text.text: Major events in the history of France.

events.headline: Earliest Settlements
events.text: The first human settlements in what is now France date back to around 5000 BC, with evidence of agriculture and permanent dwellings.

events.headline: Celtic Tribes
events.text: By 600 BC, Celtic tribes, known as the Gauls, inhabited the region, establishing a rich culture and social structure.

events.headline: Roman Conquest of Gaul
events.text: Julius Caesar completed the conquest of Gaul in 51 BC, integrating the region into the Roman Empire and leading to significant cultural changes.

events.headline: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
events.text: The fall of the Western Roman Empire marked the beginning of the Middle Ages in France, leading to the rise of feudalism.

events.headline: Treaty of Verdun
events.text: The Treaty of Verdun divided the Carolingian Empire into three kingdoms, laying the groundwork for modern France and Germany.

events.headline: Hugh Capet Becomes King
events.text: Hugh Capet was elected king, marking the beginning of the Capetian dynasty which would rule France for over 800 years.

events.headline: Start of the Hundred Years' War
events.text: The conflict between England and France over territorial claims began, lasting until 1453 and significantly shaping both nations.

events.headline: Joan of Arc's Campaign
events.text: Joan of Arc led French forces to several important victories during the Hundred Years' War, becoming a national heroine.

events.headline: Francis I Becomes King
events.text: Francis I's reign marked the Renaissance in France, characterized by cultural flourishing and the strengthening of royal power.

events.headline: French Wars of Religion
events.text: A series of conflicts between Catholics and Protestants (Huguenots) erupted, leading to widespread violence and political instability.

events.headline: Edict of Nantes
events.text: The Edict of Nantes granted religious freedom to Huguenots, helping to end the French Wars of Religion and promote civil peace.

events.headline: Louis XIV Ascends the Throne
events.text: Louis XIV, known as the Sun King, began his reign, which would become synonymous with absolute monarchy and the centralization of power.

events.headline: French Revolution Begins
events.text: The storming of the Bastille marked the beginning of the French Revolution, a period of radical social and political upheaval.

events.headline: Execution of Louis XVI
events.text: King Louis XVI was executed by guillotine, symbolizing the end of the monarchy and the rise of republicanism in France.

events.headline: Napoleon Becomes Emperor
events.text: Napoleon Bonaparte crowned himself Emperor of the French, initiating a series of military campaigns across Europe.

events.headline: Battle of Waterloo
events.text: Napoleon's defeat at the Battle of Waterloo marked the end of his rule and the restoration of the Bourbon monarchy.

events.headline: Franco-Prussian War
events.text: The Franco-Prussian War resulted in the defeat of France and the proclamation of the German Empire, leading to significant territorial losses.

events.headline: World War I Begins
events.text: France entered World War I following the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, leading to four years of devastating conflict.

events.headline: Fall of France in World War II
events.text: Nazi Germany invaded France, leading to the swift defeat of French forces and the establishment of the Vichy regime.

events.headline: D-Day: Allied Invasion
events.text: The Allied invasion of Normandy on D-Day marked the beginning of the liberation of France from Nazi occupation.

events.headline: Fifth Republic Established
events.text: The establishment of the Fifth Republic, led by Charles de Gaulle, marked a new era in French politics and governance.

events.headline: Euro Introduced
events.text: France adopted the Euro as its official currency, marking a significant step in European economic integration.

events.headline: Paris Attacks
events.text: A series of coordinated terrorist attacks in Paris resulted in significant loss of life and heightened security concerns across Europe.

events.headline: COVID-19 Lockdown
events.text: France implemented a nationwide lockdown in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, affecting daily life and the economy.
